did.head: Descriptive Summary
did.unittitle: Criminal charges records of the Auditor of Public Accounts, 1784-1905

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Virginia Auditor of Public Accounts. Criminal charges records, 1784-1905. Accession APA 715. State government records collection, The Library of Virginia, Richmond, Virginia.

bioghist.head: Biographical Information
bioghist.p: On 3 January 1788 the General Assembly passed an act authorizing the reimbursement by the state of expenses incurred by individuals in the apprehension, trial, and punishment of criminals. Clerks of state and local courts forwarded the names of jurors, witnesses and other claimants with accounts of their expenses to the auditor for certification and payment. The state also paid local officials and private citizens for questioning, guarding, feeding, and transporting prisoners to the local jail or the state penitentiary.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Criminal charges records, 1784-1905, of the Auditor of Public Accounts are housed in 76 boxes and 10 volumes. Included are accounts, certificates, correspondence, receipts, and vouchers relating to the repayment of expenses incurred by individuals in the apprehension, trial, and punishment of criminals. Clerks of state and local courts forwarded the names of jurors, witnesses and other claimants with accounts of their expenses to the auditor for certification and payment. The records often include the criminals name, locality, nature of crime, and itemized information on charges accrued. Of note included are records relating to enslaved and free African Americans.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection is arranged into the following series:

list.item: Series I: Jurors and witnesses, State and Local Courts [Chronological]
Series II: Jurors and witnesses, Localities [Alphabetical]
Series IV: Guards for prisoners, Expenses
Series V: Officers of courts, Expenses

did.unittitle: Series I: Jurors and witnesses, State and Local Courts, 1784-1818, 1861-1868.

scopecontent.p: Series I: Jurors and witnesses, State and Local Courts, 1784-1818, 1861-1868, includes certificates, receipts, and vouchers housed in 15 boxes and arranged chronologically. Clerks of state and local courts forwarded the names of jurors, witnesses, and other claimants with accounts of their expenses to the auditor for certification and payment. The state also paid local officials and private citizens for guarding, feeding, questioning, and transporting prisoners to the local jail or the state penitentiary.

Included are accounts for attending court as a witness, capturing and guarding prisoners, feeding and clothing prisoners, travel expenses, executing peace warrants, hiring of horses, travelling to compare polls for congressional elections, and other fees. The records include the name of the person attending court, name and offense of the defendant, date and location of court, time spent at court, and rate and fees due. The offenses include charges of murder, forgery, horse stealing, larceny, mutilation, rape, burglary, hog stealing, indecency, breach of peace, and drunk and riotous conduct, among others.

Of note, many of these records include information on cases against enslaved and free African Americans. Included is the name of the defendant, their locality of origin, nature of crime, as well as the name and locality of the enslavers. The records, 1861-1863, are primarily from West Virginia counties, though there are a few from Virginia areas (Accomack County; Alexandria) and the records, 1868, are only from Virginia counties.
Series I and Series II include the same types of materials, with Series I including materials mainly from 1784-1818, while Series II including materials mainly from 1823-1883.

did.unittitle: Series II: Jurors and witnesses, Localities, 1799-1883.

scopecontent.p: Series II: Jurors and witnesses records, Localities, 1799-1883, includes certificates, receipts, and vouchers housed in 51 boxes and arranged alphabetically by locality. Clerks of state and local courts forwarded the names of jurors, witnesses, and other claimants with accounts of their expenses to the auditor for certification and payment. The state also paid local officials and private citizens for guarding, feeding, questioning, and transporting prisoners to the local jail or the state penitentiary.

Included are accounts for attending court as a witness, capturing and guarding prisoners, feeding and clothing prisoners, travel expenses, executing peace warrants, hiring of horses, travelling to compare polls for congressional elections, and other fees. The records include the name of the person attending court, name and offense of the defendant, date and location of court, time spent at court, and rate and fees due. The offenses include charges of murder, forgery, horse stealing, larceny, mutilation, rape, burglary, hog stealing, indecency, breach of peace, and drunk and riotous conduct, among others.

Of note, many of these records include information on cases against enslaved and free African Americans. Included is the name of the defendant, their locality of origin, nature of crime, as well as the name and locality of the enslavers.

did.unittitle: Henrico County and Richmond,1829 June, October-November

scopecontent.p: Series III: Penitentiary expenses, 1809-1891, are housed in 6 boxes and arranged chronologically. Included are accounts submitted for charges for transporting prisoners to the penitentiary, guarding prisoners before transportation, hiring of horses and forage, the purchase of handcuffs and provisions for prisoners, and other costs. The accounts list the prisoners name, crime, and costs associated for guarding and transporting the prisoner(s) to the State penitentiary in Richmond, Virginia. Included are accounts relating to enslaved and free people of color.

Series IV: Guard expenses, 1796-1799, 1849-1851, are housed in 4 boxes and arranged chronologically. The accounts submitted to the Auditor of Public Accounts were for charges for guarding prisoners (including the name of the guard, locality, prisoners name), daily fees, and sometimes the crime the prisoner committed. Included are charges for guarding enslaved persons, their names, and their enslavers names. These are not the only records relating to guard expenses as they can be found throughout the previous series, but for some reason these were grouped together and the archivist maintained the original order.

did.unittitle: Series V: Officers of Court, Expenses, 1822-1905.

scopecontent.p: Series V: Officers of Court, Expenses, 1822-1905, are housed in 2 boxes and arranged alphabetically by folder title. Included are miscellaneous expenses paid to officers of the court (attorney, clerk, judge, and witnesses fees). Similarly to Series IV, these are not the only records relating to court expenses as they can be found throughout the previous series. For some reason these records were grouped together and the archivist maintained the original order.

did.unittitle: Allowances for judges and attorneys for the Commonwealth, 1822-1865

scopecontent.p: Series VI: Ledgers, 1884-1928, arranged chronologically into 10 volumes and within the volume alphabetically by locality.
